messages:
maria: Quick update — canary finished for the SWF micro-batcher rollout. p99 latency for short-chat traffic down ~28%, token cost down ~19% across the canary fleet. rolling to 60% now. :tada:
kevin: amazing! can you drop the top-line numbers and the dashboard link?
maria: sure — p50 -14%, p95 -21%, p99 -28%. cost/unit (tokens) ~19% reduction. dashboard: https://console.redwood/perf/swf-canary (can view perf by model & route)
anya: congrats! any regressions on long-seq workloads or embeddings?
maria: good q — we saw a slight increase in 99th for >1024 tokens on a small subset (+4%), suspected because SWF favors smaller windows. we added a route-based policy to skip SWF for long-seq models during canary.
sanjay: do we have the canary flush logs? want to confirm tail latencies during spikes.
maria: pasted a snippet from canary logs: ```
# sample aggregated tail logs (canary node)
2026-03-22T21:34:10Z p99=312ms p95=92ms p50=18ms tokens=382 avg_bsz=4.6
2026-03-22T21:35:10Z p99=305ms p95=89ms p50=17ms tokens=401 avg_bsz=4.8
# end
```
kevin: nice. what's the rollout plan? can we hit 100% tonight?
maria: plan: 60% now, monitor for 3h (alerts on p99 > 1.2x baseline or errors > 0.5%), then 85% after signoff, 100% in 12-18h if stable. ops page updated with alert thresholds.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout: swf-microbatcher -> 60% (started by maria) — status: healthy. :white_check_mark:
anya: tagging @sre to watch the p99 policies. also we should add a quicknote to the release changelog about SWF and route opt-outs.
maria: already added in /releases/notes and pinged product for a customer-facing blurb.
sanjay: cost numbers are compelling — any plan to expose an opt-in toggle for customers who want to force SWF?
maria: yes, roadmap ticket created (ENG-1348) to add per-tenant batching policy; will start with internal beta.
kevin: thanks — can we get a short exec summary for the weekly update? 2 lines: impact + next steps.
maria: on it — will DM you the summary. :+1:
